title: Represented epimorphisms give local lifts on the pro-etale site in their value universe
statement: Let X be a scheme in universe u and mu:A to B a morphism of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume the induced map between represented Type-u-valued sheaves is an epimorphism. For every site object T and map g:T to B, there is a covering sieve S on T such that every f:V to T in S admits t:V to A with t mu=f g. The epi hypothesis stays in the represented-sheaf universe; it is not replaced by an epimorphism of universe-lifted sheaves.

source.place: Tag 00WN, epi/local-surjectivity criterion, with the pro-etale site Tag 098K and bounded affine weakly contractible refinements Tags 098I and 0990

proof.text: Use the pro-etale affine weakly contractible covering family, and refine an affine base by a fixed small such cover. On each compact projective cover, any covering family refines to a finite clopen partition: lift its represented covering epimorphism into the sheaf coproduct and read the locally constant component indices; compactness makes the partition finite. Partitions of the fixed small scheme form a small type.

Compute the associated-sheaf refinement colimits on these small partition diagrams and descend along the fixed affine covers. Matching families and equalizers remain small, giving associated sheaves in the Type-u value universe. The usual finite-limit argument makes this adjunction left exact; this is the size justification required to apply the set-sheaf epi criterion to the displayed represented map.

Apply the epi/local-surjectivity criterion to the represented map. The image sieve of g is covering. By Yoneda its membership at f is precisely the existence of a t with t mu=f g, so choosing that sieve proves the conclusion. No object is defined by choosing this merely existing sieve.

lean.statement:
theorem representable_epi_local_lifting
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A B : X.ProEt} (μ : A ⟶ B)
    (hμ : Epi ((topology X).yoneda.map μ)) (T : X.ProEt) (g : T ⟶ B) :
    ∃ S : Sieve T, S ∈ topology X T ∧
      ∀ (V : X.ProEt) (f : V ⟶ T), S f → ∃ t : V ⟶ A, t ≫ μ = f ≫ g
